content.title: Lipid-lowering therapy in ACS patients
content.figure: Flowchart (Figure 18) showing lipid-lowering therapy algorithm for acute coronary syndrome (ACS) patients
content.key_thresholds: LDL-C < 1.4 mmol/L (or 55 mg/dL); consider LDL-C <1.0 mmol/L if recurrent event
content.inpatient_algorithm_summary: During admission: For LLT-naive patients initiate high-potency high-dose statin (Class I). For patients on low-potency/low-dose statin change to high-potency high-dose statin (Class I). For patients already on highest tolerated statin, assess LDL-C: if LDL-C >=1.4 mmol/L (55 mg/dL) add ezetimibe (Class I); if LDL-C remains >=1.4 mmol/L on statin + ezetimibe add PCSK9 inhibitor (Class I).
content.outpatient_follow_up: After 4-6 weeks: check LDL-C. If LDL-C <1.4 mmol/L (55 mg/dL) no change. If not at target, on highest tolerated statin add ezetimibe; if already on statin + ezetimibe and LDL-C still >=1.4 mmol/L, add PCSK9 inhibitor. Reassess after further 4-6 weeks and proceed similarly.
content.abbreviations_and_notes: ACS = acute coronary syndrome; LDL-C = low-density lipoprotein cholesterol; LLT = lipid-lowering therapy; PCSK9i = proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 inhibitor.
content.source_notes: Adapted from figure caption and accompanying guideline text. Emphasis on escalation: statin → ezetimibe → PCSK9 inhibitor for persistent LDL-C above goal.

Associated Conditions: Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) patients with elevated LDL-C
Persistent elevated LDL-C / hypercholesterolemia despite statin ± ezetimibe
genes.context: PCSK9 inhibitors (PCSK9i) are recommended (Class I) to be added when LDL-C remains ≥1.4 mmol/L (55 mg/dL) despite highest tolerated statin and ezetimibe; term 'PCSK9i' and full name 'proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 inhibitor' appear in the figure and caption.
